title: Cost-Aware SGD: Theory and Applications to LLM Policy Optimization
claim: Our cost-aware method reaches peak accuracy with far fewer tokens than the baseline, showing a large efficiency gain.
layout: 1 panel line plot, left-to-right, dotted guides with double-arrow annotations of savings
description: A single line chart titled "Accuracy vs. Token Count (Qwen3-8B)". The x-axis is cumulative tokens, from 0 to about 440M. The y-axis is accuracy in percent, from about 33 to 60. Two curves with markers are shown. The blue GRPO baseline rises slowly and plateaus near 58–59%. The orange CA-GRPO curve sits above it and ends at about 59% near 213M tokens. Horizontal dotted lines in both colors mark the peak accuracy level. Vertical gray dotted lines drop from the key points. A black double-headed arrow labeled "(1) 17% fewer tokens" and a longer gray arrow labeled "(2) 51% fewer tokens" show the token savings. A legend titled "Method" sits at the right. The eye goes first to the orange curve, then to the bold annotations.
caption: Qwen3-8B training with GRPO and Cost-Aware GRPO (CA-GRPO). We evaluate on AIME1983-2024 (pass@1/mean@32) and report cumulative tokens used in policy gradient computation. We plot every $20$ training steps until peak accuracy is attained for both. CA-GRPO requires: (1) 17% fewer tokens to reach its absolute peak than GRPO requires to come within 2% of that performance, (2) 51% fewer tokens to match or exceed the peak accuracy of GRPO.
abstract: We consider the problem of Cost-Aware Learning, where sampling different components of a finite-sum objective incurs different costs. The objective is to reach a target error while minimizing the total cost. We propose Cost-Aware SGD, which uses a distribution based on gradient norms and costs to sample components. We provide a thorough analysis of this algorithm, including cost-improvement bounds over baselines, a characterization of distribution proxy sub-optimality, and a lower bound. We apply our theoretical insights to reinforcement learning with language models, where the cost of including a sequence in a policy-gradient update scales with its length. We find that advantage magnitude is a high-fidelity proxy for sequence-level gradient norms, motivating Cost-Aware GRPO. Across 1.5B, 4B, and 8B LLMs, Cost-Aware GRPO matches or exceeds baseline accuracy while using up to 33\% fewer policy-optimization FLOPs and 33\% fewer total FLOPs.
